output.rationale: Teach the two confirmed derivative-rule gaps with one compact model, then check each rule in its own step and end with delayed retrieval.

coverage.focus: Derivative rule basics for products and composites
essentialIdeas: The product rule differentiates a product by adding the derivative of the first factor times the second factor and the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.
The chain rule differentiates a composite function by multiplying the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.
completionEvidence: State when the product rule is required and apply it to one product.
State how the chain rule fits a composite function and apply it once.

evidenceMap.essentialIdea: The product rule differentiates a product by adding the derivative of the first factor times the second factor and the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.
The chain rule differentiates a composite function by multiplying the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a compact model, explain the rule in your own words, repair any missing step, then explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining and repairing the relationship helps turn a rule into a usable mental model.
how: Read the model once for the big picture.
Answer from memory in plain language.
Use feedback to fix the specific gap.
Explain again with the corrected rule.
Finish with a delayed retrieval check.
methodBriefing.completion: You complete the lesson by attempting every required question and giving a correct final explanation or application.
personalization: Start with the overall model before details.
Use one visible step at a time.
Restore support in smaller pieces after a miss.

activities.label: model_product_rule
activities.title: Product rule basics
activities.body: Read the model. Then get ready to explain it in your own words.

essentialIdeas: The product rule differentiates a product by adding the derivative of the first factor times the second factor and the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.

activities.label: explain_product_rule
activities.title: Explain the product rule
activities.body: Say the rule in your own words. Keep it to one short explanation.
activities.correctAnswer: When two functions are multiplied, differentiate one factor at a time and add the two parts: first derivative times second, plus first times second derivative.
activities.feedback: A complete answer says the rule is for a product and includes both terms. If you only describe one factor, repair that missing second part.

activities.label: repair_product_rule
activities.title: Fix the product rule step
activities.body: Revise your answer using the full two-term rule. Keep the correction brief.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking the derivative of a product is just the derivative of the first factor times the second factor, or just multiply the derivatives.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is first derivative times second plus first times second derivative.
activities.feedback: The missing correction is that both terms are needed. One derivative alone is not enough for a product.

activities.label: model_chain_rule
activities.title: Chain rule basics
activities.body: Read the model. Then prepare to explain how the two parts work together.

essentialIdeas: The chain rule differentiates a composite function by multiplying the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.

activities.label: check_chain_rule
activities.title: Which rule fits this form?
activities.body: Choose the rule that matches a composite function.
choices: The chain rule: differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the inner derivative.
The product rule: differentiate each factor and add the results.
The quotient rule: differentiate the top and bottom, then divide.
The power rule: bring the exponent down and subtract one.
activities.correctAnswer: The chain rule: differentiate the outer function, then multiply by the inner derivative.
activities.feedback: A composite function needs the chain rule because one function is inside another. The other rules fit different derivative structures.

activities.label: reexplain_chain_rule
activities.title: Restate the chain rule
activities.body: State the chain rule again in your own words.
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, take the derivative of the outside function at the inside function, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
activities.feedback: A complete restatement names the outer part, the inner part, and the multiplication step. If you miss one layer, add it back.

The chain rule differentiates a composite function by multiplying the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function by the inner derivative.

items.essentialIdea: Product rule differentiates a product by adding u'v and uv'.

check.title: Differentiate a product
check.prompt: How do you differentiate a product of two functions?
check.referenceAnswer: If y=uv, then dy/dx=u'v+uv'. Differentiate the first factor times the second, then the first times the derivative of the second.
check.feedback: It uses two terms, not one combined derivative.

items.essentialIdea: Chain rule differentiates a composite by multiplying outer and inner derivatives.

check.title: Differentiate a composite
check.prompt: How do you differentiate a composite function f(g(x))?
check.referenceAnswer: Differentiate the outer function at g(x), then multiply by g'(x). In symbols, d/dx f(g(x))=f'(g(x))g'(x).
check.feedback: The outer derivative is evaluated at the inner function, then multiplied by the inner derivative.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify the chain rule
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which derivative rule applies to a composite function f(g(x))?
choices: Multiply the outer derivative by the inner derivative.
Add the derivatives of the two factors.
Differentiate each factor and multiply the results.
Take the derivative of the inner function only.
recognitionCheck.correctAnswer: Multiply the outer derivative by the inner derivative.
recognitionCheck.feedback: That is the chain rule for a composite function.

items.essentialIdea: map transforms each array element into a new value without removing items.

check.title: Map transforms elements
check.prompt: When should you use map on an array?
check.referenceAnswer: Use map when you want a new array with each element transformed into another value. It keeps the same number of items.
check.feedback: Map changes values element by element, not the array length.

items.essentialIdea: filter keeps only array elements that satisfy a condition, unlike map or reduce.

check.title: Filter keeps matches
check.prompt: When should you use filter on an array?
check.referenceAnswer: Use filter when you want a new array containing only the elements that meet a condition. It removes items that do not match.
check.feedback: Filter selects items by a test, rather than transforming every item.

recognitionCheck.title: Pick the right method
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which method should you use to turn each number in an array into its square?
recognitionCheck.feedback: Squaring each element is a one-to-one transformation, which is map.
